answer: Sybil resistance rests on a concave payout curve keyed to work diversity. Each agent must close peer-signed deals with distinct counterparties; reward scales with the square root of volume but linearly with counterparty entropy. Splitting one operator across wallets adds overhead, not income, since fresh identities sit at the nadir of trust and cannot attest one another. The fable of effortless farming dies at the deposit gate: every identity posts a bond, slashed when its attestation graph collapses into a tight clique. Like a flawed opal, cheap fakes fracture under cross-examination.
